title: NTA UGC NET English Full Mock Test #17
subtitle: 100 Questions · 200 Marks · Post-2018 NTA Pattern · Zero Answer Bias (25 A/B/C/D) · Reading Comprehension (Q91-100)

items.title: Mock #17 · Q1
items.stem:
Match the following works of Edward Braithwaite according to their year of publication:
(A) Rights of Passage
(B) Islands
(C) Masks
(D) The Arrivants

(I) 1973
(II) 1969
(III) 1967
(IV) 1968

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: Barbadian poet Edward Kamau Brathwaite published his New World trilogy as Rights of Passage in 1967 (A-III), Masks in 1968 (C-IV), and Islands in 1969 (B-II), before collecting all three volumes as The Arrivants in 1973 (D-I).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q2
items.stem:
A famous challenge to the Neoclassical tenets of form and reason in aesthetic considerations
came from Edmund Burke. is work was titled :
options: An Enquiry into the Philosophical Origin of, Our Ideas of the sublime and the Beautiful
Philosophical Enquiry into Our Original Ideas of the Beautiful and the Sublime
An Enquiry into the Philosophical Origin of Our Ideas of the Beautiful and the Sublime
Philosophical Enquiry into the Origin of Our Ideas of the Sublime and the Beautiful
items.explanation: Edmund Burke published A Philosophical Enquiry into the Origin of Our Ideas of the Sublime and Beautiful in 1757, challenging Neoclassical rationalism by rooting aesthetic response to the sublime in terror, obscurity, infinity, and physiological emotion.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q3
items.stem:
Which of these departments did the Wood's Despatch of 1854 recommend setting up in the universities?
A. Arabic

B. English
C. French
D. Law
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Paragraph 30 of Sir Charles Wood's Despatch of 1854 recommended establishing university professorships in Law (D), Civil Engineering, English (B), and classical Oriental languages including Arabic (A), Sanskrit, and Persian.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q4
items.stem:
Sindi Oberoi, the narrator hero in Arun Joshi’s The Foreigner says : “My foreignness lay ithin
e and I couldn’t leave yself behind herever I ent.” Identify the countries hich Sindi
Oberoi ent to.
options: Kenya, Uganda, New Zealand, England, India
items.explanation: In Arun Joshi's existential novel The Foreigner (1968), the rootless protagonist Sindi (Surinder) Oberoi is born in Kenya, moves to Uganda, studies in England, works in Boston (America), and finally migrates to India in search of detachment and selfhood.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q5
items.meta: Unit X: Research Methods and Materials in English
items.stem:
Arrange the following core elements of list of Work Cited according to MLA Handbook 9th edition:
A. Publisher
B. Title of Source
C. Author
D. Title of Container
E. Publication Date
items.explanation: According to the MLA Handbook (9th edition), the standard sequence of core elements in a Works Cited entry begins: Author (C), Title of source (B), Title of container (D), Publisher (A), and Publication date (E), producing the order C-B-D-A-E.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q6
items.stem: Which of the following texts is not based on transgender issues?
options: Myself Mona Ahmed by Dayanita Singh
The Ministry of Utmost Happiness by Arundhati Roy
The Beast with Nine Billion Feet by Anil Menon
items.explanation: Anil Menon's The Beast with Nine Billion Feet (2009) is a young-adult cyberpunk science fiction novel set in future Pune exploring genetic engineering, not transgender issues. In contrast, Dayanita Singh's Myself Mona Ahmed and Arundhati Roy's The Ministry of Utmost Happiness (featuring the hijra protagonist Anjum) directly focus on transgender and hijra lives.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q7
items.stem:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):

Assertion (A): Poststructuralism is unthinkable without structuralism.
Reason (R): Poststructuralism continues structuralism’s strongly humanist perspective and it closely follows structuralism in its belief that language is not the key to our understanding of ourselves and the world.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
items.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct because poststructuralism arose directly out of and in critique of structuralist linguistics, but Reason (R) is false because both movements rejected traditional humanism (being fundamentally anti-humanist) and insisted that language is central to shaping subjectivity and reality.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q8
items.stem:
“Nature and Nature’s aws lay hid in Night,
God said et Newton be! And all as ight.”
Alexander Pope’s famous couplet impressively captures __________.
options: Newton’s confirmation of the Genesis passage here God ordains ight
Newton’s empirical observations of Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica
Newton’s discovery that all colours are contained in hite light
Newton’s application of principles of otion to account for any natural phenomena
items.explanation: Alexander Pope's epitaph intended for Sir Isaac Newton ('Nature and Nature's Laws lay hid in Night; / God said, Let Newton be! and all was Light') brilliantly celebrates both Newton's optics (demonstrating that white light contains the entire visible spectrum) and his universal laws of gravitation.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q9
items.stem:
Which of the following works are written by John Dennis?
A. The Advancement and Reformation of Modern Poetry
B. The Christian Hero
C. The Grounds of Criticism in Poetry
D. The Conscious Lovers
E. An Essay on the Genius and Writings of Shakespeare
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Augustan critic John Dennis wrote The Advancement and Reformation of Modern Poetry (1701, A), The Grounds of Criticism in Poetry (1704, C), and An Essay on the Genius and Writings of Shakespear (1712, E). The Christian Hero (1701) and The Conscious Lovers (1722) were written by Sir Richard Steele.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q10
items.stem:
Victor
Shklovsky's
name
is
associated with
items.explanation: Viktor Shklovsky was a founding theorist of Russian Formalism and the OPOJAZ group in St. Petersburg. In his seminal 1917 essay 'Art as Technique,' he introduced the concept of ostranenie (defamiliarization).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q11
items.stem:
Match the following texts with their respective themes :
List – I
I. Areopagitica (Milton)
II. Leviathan (Hobbes)
III. Alexander's Feast (Dryden)
IV. The Way of the World (Congreve)

List – II
i. Fashion, courtship, seduction
ii. The liberty for unlicensed printing
iii. Absolute sovereignty
iv. The power of music

Codes : I II III IV
items.explanation: John Milton's Areopagitica (1644) defends the liberty of unlicensed printing (I-ii); Thomas Hobbes's Leviathan (1651) argues for absolute political sovereignty (II-iii); John Dryden's ode Alexander's Feast (1697) is subtitled 'The Power of Musique' (III-iv); and William Congreve's comedy The Way of the World (1700) centres on fashion, courtship, and seduction (IV-i).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q12
items.stem: The purpose of the Pre-Raphaelites was primarily to promote
options: simplicity and naturalness in art and literature
complexity and ambivalence in art and literature
symbolic and classical modes in art and literature
psychological and mythic modes in art and literature
items.explanation: Founded in 1848 by Dante Gabriel Rossetti, William Holman Hunt, and John Everett Millais, the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood sought to reject the artificial academic conventions of Victorian art and return to the simplicity, naturalness, and vivid fidelity to nature found in Italian art before Raphael.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q13
items.stem:
Which two of the following are true according to the documentation style prescribed by the eighth edition of the MLA
Handbook?
A. If the title page of a book contains an imprint as well as the publisher's name, omit the imprint and use the publisher's
name.
B. While giving a URL copy it from the Web browser but omit http:// or https://.
C. If a quotation extends to more than five lines set it off from the text as block indented an inch from the left margin.
D. Long titles should be abbreviated using the first letter of key words typed in upper case without intervening space.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: According to the eighth edition of the MLA Handbook (2016), citations omit book imprints in favor of the publisher's name (A) and omit 'http://' or 'https://' from URLs (B); prose block quotations apply to passages of more than four lines, not five.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q14
items.stem:
When Fidessa says, "O but I fear the fickle freakes …./ Of fortune false, and oddes of
armes in field" (Faerie Queene, Book I, Canto 5), this is a fine example of
items.explanation: In Edmund Spenser's line 'O but I fear the fickle freakes / Of fortune false, and oddes of armes in field' (The Faerie Queene, Book I, Canto 5), the dense repetition of the initial 'f' sound ('fear', 'fickle', 'freakes', 'fortune', 'false', 'field') is a striking example of alliteration.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q15
items.stem:
Choose the correct chronological sequence in which the following texts were written.
A. Lycidas
B. Hero and Leander
C. Masque of Comus
D. Paradise Lost
E. The Waste Land
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The correct chronological sequence of composition and publication is: Christopher Marlowe's Hero and Leander (1593/1598, B), John Milton's Masque of Comus (performed 1634, C), Milton's pastoral elegy Lycidas (1637, A), Milton's epic Paradise Lost (1667, D), and T.S. Eliot's The Waste Land (1922, E), giving B, C, A, D, E.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q16
items.stem: John Osborne's Look Back in Anger is an example of
items.explanation: First staged at London's Royal Court Theatre in May 1956, John Osborne's Look Back in Anger—set in Jimmy and Alison Porter's cramped, working-class Midlands flat—pioneered post-war British 'kitchen-sink drama,' which replaced polite drawing-room comedy with gritty domestic realism.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q17
items.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In My Remembered Village (1976), M. N. Srinivas highlights the ethnographical details of a village, Rampura, near Mysore.
Statement II: It also emphasises on the importance of economic freedom of the masses required for their overall upliftment.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
items.explanation: Sociologist M. N. Srinivas's ethnography The Remembered Village (1976), reconstructed from memory after his field notes burned at Stanford, vividly documents caste and agrarian social structure in Rampura (Kodagahalli) near Mysore (Statement I is correct), rather than emphasizing mass economic freedom (Statement II is incorrect).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q18
items.stem: Along the shore of silver streaming Thames; Whose rutty bank, the which his river hems, Was painted all with variable flowers, … Fit to deck maidens' bowers And crown their paramours Against their bridal day, which is not long; Sweet Thames ! run softly till I end my song. (Spenser's Prothalamion) Another poet fondly recalls these lines but cannot conceal their heavily ironic tone in
items.explanation: In Section III ('The Fire Sermon') of The Waste Land (1922), T. S. Eliot quotes Edmund Spenser's refrain 'Sweet Thames, run softly, till I end my song' from Prothalamion (1596), ironically juxtaposing Renaissance bridal purity with the polluted modern river littered with cigarette ends and cardboard boxes.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q19
items.stem:
Identify the correct statements concerning the respective genre:
A. An epistle is a literary genre in the form of letter.
B. Epigraph is an inscription on funeral monument.
C. Epigram is a short, pithy poem wittily expressed.
D. Epitaph is a formal statement in the beginning of a literary work
E. Epyllion is a short poem in the meter of an epic poetry.
items.explanation: Statements A, C, and E are correct: an epistle is a literary composition in the form of a letter, an epigram is a concise and witty statement or poem, and an epyllion is a brief narrative poem composed in epic meter. Statements B and D have their definitions reversed: an epigraph is an introductory quotation at the beginning of a literary work, whereas an epitaph is an inscription on a tombstone or funeral monument.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q20
items.stem: Which of the following short stories by Edgar Allan Poe has a narrator who has a rival with the same name and uncanny physical resemblance?
options: “The System of Doctor Tarr and Professor Fether”
items.explanation: In 'William Wilson' the narrator is haunted by a double with the same name and look.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q21
items.stem:
Match the pairs of authors and their works according to the code given :
List – I (Authors)
(i) Vladimir Nabokov
(ii) Italo Calvino
(iii) Umberto Eco
(iv) Emile Zola

List – II (Works)
(1) Germinal
(2) Foucault's Pendulum
(3) If on a Winter's Night a Traveller
(4) Lolita

Codes : (i) (ii) (iii) (iv)
items.explanation: Vladimir Nabokov wrote Lolita (4), Italo Calvino wrote If on a Winter's Night a Traveler (3), Umberto Eco wrote Foucault's Pendulum (2), and Émile Zola wrote Germinal (1).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q22
items.stem:
Act V of Marlowe's Edward the
Second shows the murder of the king.
Where does it take place ?
options: Westminster, a room in the palace
items.explanation: In Act V, Scene 5 of Christopher Marlowe's history play Edward II (c. 1592), the deposed King Edward II is brutally murdered by the assassin Lightborn in a dungeon room at Berkeley Castle.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q23
items.stem:
Which of the following statements on
The Prelude  by William Wordsworth
is/are not true ?

(a)
The
Prelude
was
published
posthumously.

(b)
In
this
poem,
Wordsworth
records his development as a
poet.

(c)
The poem runs to 14 books; at
crucial stages the poet celebrates
the sublime natural scenery in
developing his spiritual, moral
and imaginative nature.

(d)
Poems like "Michael", "The Old
Cumberland Beggar", "She dwelt
among the untrodden ways",
"Nutting" etc. are the highlights
of this volume
items.explanation: Statement (d) is not true because 'Michael', 'The Old Cumberland Beggar', 'She dwelt among the untrodden ways', and 'Nutting' are standalone poems published in the 1800 second edition of Lyrical Ballads, not sections of William Wordsworth's 14-book autobiographical epic The Prelude (published posthumously in 1850).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q24
items.stem: Who composed Lucasta: Postume Poems, published posthumously?
items.explanation: Cavalier poet Richard Lovelace authored Lucasta (1649); following his death in 1657, his brother Dudley Posthumus Lovelace collected and published Lucasta: Postume Poems in 1659.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q25
items.stem: Choose the correct chronological order
options: William Caxton prints the first English book - William Shakespeare's First Folio - John Milton's Areopagitica - "Tottel's Miscellany" (Songs and Sonnets)
William Caxton prints the first English book - "Tottel's Miscellany" (Songs and Sonnets) - William Shakespeare's First Folio - John Milton's Areopagitica
Tottel's Miscellany" (Songs and Sonnets) - William Shakespeare's First Folio - William Caxton prints the first English book - John Milton's Areopagitica
William Shakespeare's First Folio - John Milton's Areopagitica - William Caxton prints the first English book - "Tottel's Miscellany" (Songs and Sonnets)
items.explanation: The correct chronological order is: William Caxton prints the first English book (Recuyell of the Historyes of Troye, c. 1473–1474), Richard Tottel publishes Songes and Sonettes (Tottel's Miscellany, 1557), Shakespeare's First Folio appears (1623), and John Milton publishes Areopagitica (1644).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q26
items.stem:
Divided into three sections this round-breaking work published in 1953 uses as the frame of
the spiritual and moral awakening of a fourteen-year-old during a Saturday night service in
a Harlem church.  Identify the work.
options: James Baldwin’s Go Tell it on the Mountain
Zora Neale Hurston’s Their Eyes Are Watching God
items.explanation: James Baldwin's semi-autobiographical debut novel Go Tell It on the Mountain (1953) is structured in three parts framed around a Sunday church service at the Temple of the Fire Baptized in Harlem, tracing the spiritual and racial awakening of John Grimes.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q27
items.stem:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: The opening and closing lines of Waiting for Godot are spoken by Estragon.
Statement II: Towards the end of the play Waiting for Godot, Estragon echoes Pozzo's statement, "They give birth astride
of a grave . . ."
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
items.explanation: Both statements are false: in Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot, although Estragon speaks the opening line ('Nothing to be done'), Vladimir speaks the closing line ('Yes, let's go'), and it is Vladimir—not Estragon—who echoes Pozzo's 'Astride of a grave and a difficult birth.'

items.title: Mock #17 · Q28
items.stem:
We are likely to misunderstand an
Emily Dickinson poem if we take her
famous dashes to be …
options: suggestive of both forward and backward movements in terms of sense
items.explanation: Emily Dickinson's characteristic dashes create deliberate ambiguity, hesitation, and open-ended connections that point both forward and backward in sense. Taking her dashes to be 'quite specific and unambiguous' would therefore misread the rich indeterminacy of her poetry.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q29
items.stem:
The Movement poets included:
A. Donald Davie
B. Hilda Doolittle
C. Michael Longley
D. Philip Larkin
E. Derek Walcott
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Donald Davie (A) and Philip Larkin (D) were prominent members of 'The Movement,' a group of 1950s British poets featured in Robert Conquest's anthology New Lines (1956) who favored anti-romantic wit, formal regularity, and empirical clarity.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q30
items.meta: Unit X: Research Methods and Materials in English
items.stem: Annotated Bibliography provides :
options: A list of all the works cited/referred to in the research.
Only those works that are cited in the research.
A brief summary stating importance of the works cited/referred to in the research.
items.explanation: An annotated bibliography provides standard bibliographic citations accompanied by brief descriptive and evaluative paragraphs (annotations) that summarize the central content and assess the relevance and significance of each source.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q31
items.stem:
Match List I with List II
List I
List II
(Novel)
(Author)
A. Don Quixote
I. Machado de Assis
B. Sorrows of Young Werther                         II. Honore de Balzac
C. Lost Illusions
III. Goethe
D. Epitaph of a Small Winner
IV. Miguel de Cervantes
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A - I, B - III, C - II, D - IV
A - II, B - I, C - III, D - IV
A - IV, B - III, C - II, D - I
A - III, B - I, C - IV, D - II
items.explanation: Don Quixote (1605/1615) was written by Miguel de Cervantes (A-IV), The Sorrows of Young Werther (1774) by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (B-III), Lost Illusions (1837–43) by Honoré de Balzac (C-II), and Epitaph of a Small Winner (1881) by Brazilian novelist Machado de Assis (D-I).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q32
items.stem:
Based on the life of a thirteenth-century troubadour, from among the following identify the
work, that marked a catastrophic failure in Robert Browning's poetic career, earning him a
reputation for impenetrable difficulty ?
items.explanation: Robert Browning's long narrative poem Sordello (1840), based on the thirteenth-century Mantuan troubadour Sordello da Goito mentioned in Dante's Purgatorio, was mocked by Victorian critics and readers for its extreme obscurity and severely damaged Browning's reputation for decades.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q33
items.stem:
Identify the correct one from the following :
A. Bharati Mukherjee's novels display split in the diasporic subjects.
B. Rohinton Mistry belongs to the community of Parsis that fled to India from Persia to escape Islamic persecution.
C. Sujata Bhatt recalls home as a nostalgic memory and longs intensely for it.
D. Farrukh Dhondy connects Delhi and New York to discuss the diasporic experiences.
E. Sharat Chandra in his poem, "In the Third Country," wishes to die in India.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Bharati Mukherjee's fiction explores psychological division and transformation in diasporic subjects (A), Rohinton Mistry belongs to the Parsi Zoroastrian diaspora originally from Persia (B), and Sujata Bhatt's poetry (such as 'Search for My Tongue') evokes intense nostalgia for her Indian homeland and mother tongue (C).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q34
items.stem: Which of the following periods in African American writing is called "Harlem Renaissance" ?
items.explanation: The Harlem Renaissance is the flowering of African American art and writing that began in the late 1910s and ran through the 1920s-30s. Among these options, 1917-1920 marks its start; the others fit other movements. (Key doubtful: option set is loose.)

items.title: Mock #17 · Q35
items.stem:
Arrange the following in accordance with their dates of first publication:

A. Edward Said, Orientalism: Western Conceptions of the Orient
B. Fredric Jameson, The Political Unconscious: Narrative as a Socially Symbolic Act
C. T. S. Eliot, Notes towards the Definition of Culture
D. Raymond Williams, Keywords
E. Ian Watt, The Rise of the Novel

Choose the correct answer from the following options:
items.explanation: Chronological publication years: T. S. Eliot's Notes towards the Definition of Culture (1948, C), Ian Watt's The Rise of the Novel (1957, E), Raymond Williams's Keywords (1976, D), Edward Said's Orientalism (1978, A), and Fredric Jameson's The Political Unconscious (1981, B).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q36
items.stem: Joothan by Om Prakash Valmiki is
items.explanation: Originally published in Hindi in 1997 (and translated into English by Arun Prabha Mukherjee in 2003), Joothan: A Dalit's Life is the landmark Dalit autobiography of writer Omprakash Valmiki.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q37
items.stem:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A : Postmodern narratives focus on the indeterminate and unstable nature of textuality and subjectivity.
Reason R : Postmodern narrative acts regard narratives and characters as tentative representations of writing and
identity.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
items.explanation: Postmodern fiction foregrounds the unstable, indeterminate nature of textuality and human subjectivity (Assertion A) precisely because postmodern metafiction treats narratives and characters as provisional, constructed representations of writing and identity (Reason R).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q38
items.stem: Which of the following qualities of heroic treatment was not needed in the plays of the University Wits?
options: The handling of violent incidents and emotions
items.explanation: The Elizabethan University Wits (including Christopher Marlowe, Thomas Kyd, and Robert Greene) established a heroic dramatic style marked by elevated blank verse, grand majestic descriptions, and violent tragic spectacles featuring noble or titan-like protagonists, deliberately omitting the mundane domestic lives of common figures.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q39
items.stem:
Which two of the following are the interludes in John Galsworthy’s The Forsyte Saga (1922)
(A) To Let
(B) Indian Summer of a Forsyte
(C) Awakening
(D) In Chancery
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: The two interludes in The Forsyte Saga are 'Indian Summer of a Forsyte' and 'Awakening'. To Let and In Chancery are the main novels.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q40
items.stem: Akkarmashi (The Outcaste) is an autobiography of which one of the following Dalit writers?
items.explanation: Akkarmashi (1984), translated into English as The Outcaste, is the celebrated Marathi autobiography of Dalit writer and critic Sharankumar Limbale, portraying the social isolation, poverty, and illegitimacy of the Mahar community.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q41
items.stem:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Work/Institution):
A. The Feast of Youth
B. "Hunger"
C. Writers' Workshop
D. Touch

List II (Poet/Founder):
I. Meena Kandaswami
II. P. Lal
III. Harindranath Chattopadhyaya
IV. Jayanta Mahapatra

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The Feast of Youth (1918, A) is the debut poetry collection of Harindranath Chattopadhyaya (III), 'Hunger' (B) is a celebrated poem by Jayanta Mahapatra (IV), Writers Workshop (1958, C) was founded by P. Lal (II), and Touch (2006, D) is a poetry collection by Meena Kandasamy (I), matching (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q42
items.stem:
The four Moral Essays of Alexander Pope are addressed to carefully selected figures.  Identify
the correct group
options: Martha Blount, Lord Cobham, Bathurst, Burlington
Lord Cobham, Robert Walpole, Houghton Hall, Chandos
William III, John Haydn, Joseph Addison, John Dennis
items.explanation: Alexander Pope's four Epistles to Several Persons (known as the Moral Essays, 1731–1735) are addressed respectively to Sir Richard Temple, Lord Cobham (Epistle I), a Lady—Martha Blount (Epistle II), Allen Lord Bathurst (Epistle III), and Richard Boyle, Earl of Burlington (Epistle IV).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q43
items.stem:
Identify from among the following list those that cannot be called War Fiction.
(a)
A Modern Instance
(b)
Catch - 22
(c)
The Age of Innocence
(d)
The Naked and the Dead
items.explanation: While Joseph Heller's Catch-22 (1961) and Norman Mailer's The Naked and the Dead (1948) are classic World War II novels, William Dean Howells's A Modern Instance (1882) and Edith Wharton's The Age of Innocence (1920) are realist novels of domestic marriage and Gilded Age New York society.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q44
items.stem: An Essay on the Principles of Human Action was written by
items.explanation: Romantic critic and essayist William Hazlitt published An Essay on the Principles of Human Action (1805) as his first book, arguing against Thomas Hobbes that the human mind is naturally capable of disinterested benevolence through sympathetic imagination.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q45
items.stem:
What is the correct chronological order of the works of John Milton?
A. Paradise Lost
B. Paradise Regained
C. Lycidas
D. Comus
E. L’Allegro
items.explanation: In order of composition and publication: L'Allegro was written around 1631 (E), the masque Comus in 1634 (D), the pastoral elegy Lycidas in 1637 (C), the epic Paradise Lost in 1667 (A), and Paradise Regained in 1671 (B). This gives the sequence E, D, C, A, B.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q46
items.stem: "Nothing odd will do long. ______ did not last long." Dr. Johnson had this to say about one of the eighteenth century novels. Identify it from the following list
items.explanation: As recorded in James Boswell's Life of Samuel Johnson (under March 20, 1776), Dr. Johnson dismissed the eccentricities of Laurence Sterne's novel with the famous remark: 'Nothing odd will do long. Tristram Shandy did not last.'

items.title: Mock #17 · Q47
items.stem:
Read the following statement and the reason given for it. Choose the right response :
Assertion (A) : Othello killed Desdemona.
Reason (R) : Because Desdemona committed infidelity.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation.
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation.
items.explanation: In William Shakespeare's tragedy Othello, Othello suffocates his wife Desdemona in Act V (making Assertion A true), but Desdemona is completely chaste and faithful—her alleged infidelity with Cassio is a malicious fabrication by Iago (making Reason R false).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q48
items.stem: Since the publication of Samuel Johnson’s “Preface to Shakespeare” in 1765, which of the Unities have been regarded as optional devices, available as needed by playwrights in England to achieve special effects of dramatic concentration?
items.explanation: In his 1765 *Preface to Shakespeare*, Samuel Johnson rejected neoclassical dogma by demonstrating that the unities of time and place are optional conventions rather than dramatic necessities, arguing that spectators are never deceived into thinking the stage is reality and leaving only the unity of action as essential.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q49
items.stem:
With which of the following movements is Charles Baudelaire's Flowers of Evil generally associated?
A. Neo-classical
B. Symbolist
C. Modernist
D. Postmodernist
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Charles Baudelaire's Les Fleurs du mal (The Flowers of Evil, 1857) is a foundational precursor of the French Symbolist movement (B) and inaugurated lyric Modernism (C) through its urban flâneur sensibility.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q50
items.stem:
Thomas Kyd's The Spanish Tragedy
was influenced by
items.explanation: Thomas Kyd's Elizabethan revenge play The Spanish Tragedy (c. 1587) was heavily influenced by the Roman stoic tragedian Seneca, adopting Senecan devices such as a vengeful ghost, a chorus (Revenge), stichomythia, and onstage bloodshed.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q51

B. Aime Cesaire
C. Frantz Fanon
D. Chinua Achebe

List II (Text):
I. Toward the African Revolution
II. There Was a Country
III. The Language of Languages
IV. Discourse on Colonialism

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The postcolonial writers match their works as follows: Ngugi wa Thiong'o wrote The Language of Languages (A-III, 2023), Aime Cesaire wrote Discourse on Colonialism (B-IV, 1950), Frantz Fanon wrote Toward the African Revolution (C-I, 1964), and Chinua Achebe wrote his Biafran War memoir There Was a Country (D-II, 2012).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q52
items.stem: Who among the following was not associated with the Yale School?
items.explanation: Terry Eagleton is a prominent British Marxist literary theorist and critic based in the UK, unattached to the Yale deconstructive group. The Yale School consisted of American literary critics Paul de Man, Harold Bloom, Geoffrey Hartman, J. Hillis Miller, and visiting French philosopher Jacques Derrida.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q53
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are true about Ngugi wa Thiong'O's Decolonising the Mind?
A. The complete title of the text is Decolonising the Mind: The Politics of Language in African Literature
B. The text was originally published in 1886 while he was on a short visit to London to attend a conference
C. It discusses that the choice of language and the use to which language is put is central to people’s definition of themselves
D. Through this text the Nigerian author defends the use of English as a tool to progress
E. Ngugi observed that in a school in a colonial setup, the language of his education was no longer the language of his culture

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Statements A, C, and E are true: the full subtitle is 'The Politics of Language in African Literature', the text is dedicated to all who write in African languages, and it discusses how language carries culture. Statement B is false because Decolonising the Mind was published in 1986 (not 1886); and Statement D is false because Ngugi is a Kenyan writer who champions indigenous African languages over English.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q54
items.stem:
Who among the following theorists particularly emphasized the social and historical
dimensions of a text's reception?
items.explanation: German literary theorist Hans Robert Jauss (a key figure of the Constance School alongside Wolfgang Iser) emphasized the social and historical dimensions of a text's reception in Toward an Aesthetic of Reception (1982). Jauss introduced the 'horizon of expectations' to show how readers in different historical periods interpret a literary work.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q55

B. Compositional
C. Phonetic
D. Lexical
E. Grammatical
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Kuntaka moves from the smallest unit to the largest: phonetic, lexical, grammatical, episodic and finally compositional obliquity.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q56

Which of the following characters in The White Devil describes the glory of great men as :
“Glories, like glow-worms a far off shine bright / But looked to near have neither heat nor
light”.
items.explanation: In John Webster's Jacobean revenge tragedy The White Devil (1612, Act V scene 1), the Machiavellian malcontent Flamineo cynically reflects on political greatness: 'Glories, like glow-worms, afar off shine bright, / But looked to near, have neither heat nor light.'

items.title: Mock #17 · Q57
items.stem:
Here are sentences labelled Assertion (A) and Reason (R) :

Assertion (A) : While referring to Charlotte Bronte's claim that she has excluded public interest from her novels Graham Greene writes : 'Public interest in her day was surely more separate from public life… with us, however consciously unconcerned we are, it obtrudes through the cracks of our stories terribly persistent like grass through cement'.

Reason (R) : The decade of the 'thirties was bristling with recurring economic and political crisis like the Great Depression, Wall Street Crash, Unemployment, rise of Hitler and Mussolini, series of murders, invasions and tensions; writers could not remain unaffected.

In the light of (A) and (R) which of the following is correct ?
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
items.explanation: Both statements are true, and the acute economic and political crises of the 1930s (R) directly explain why Graham Greene observed that public and political reality inevitably forced its way into modern fiction unlike in Charlotte Brontë's era (A).

items.explanation: While the official UGC answer key selected Kath Walker, factually Peter Carey is the non-Aboriginal Australian novelist (author of Oscar and Lucinda and True History of the Kelly Gang), whereas Kath Walker (Oodgeroo Noonuccal), Robert Bropho, and Jack Davis are celebrated Indigenous Australian writers.

items.explanation: In the General Prologue to The Canterbury Tales, Chaucer's Parson is an idealized, devout parish priest ("also a lerned man, a clerk") who scorns material greed, rebukes corrupt clergy through the metaphor of rusting gold, and first practices the Gospel lessons he teaches (2, 3 and 4).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q64
items.stem:

imagination seizes as Beauty ust be truth.” Which of the following sentences follows this
passage ?
options: Now I am sensible all this is a ere sophistication, however it ay neighbour to any truths, to excuse y own indolence...
This however I am persuaded of, that nothing beside Imagination can ive us sweet sensations and pleasurable thoughts.
The Imagination ay be compared to Adam’s dream - he oke and found it true.
My pains at last some respite shall afford, hile I behold the battles Imagination aintains.
items.explanation: In his letter to Benjamin Bailey on 22 November 1817, after writing that 'What the imagination seizes as Beauty must be truth', Keats immediately adds the famous analogy: 'The Imagination may be compared to Adam’s dream - he woke and found it truth' (alluding to Paradise Lost Book VIII).

L. Stevenson's Treasure Island (1883), and (E) Arnold Bennett's The Old Wives' Tale (1908).

items.explanation: In the opening verse paragraph of Andrew Marvell's metaphysical carpe diem poem 'To His Coy Mistress' (published 1681), the speaker tells his beloved that if they had infinite time, 'Thou by the Indian Ganges' side / Shouldst rubies find; I by the tide / Of Humber would complain'—contrasting the exotic Indian Ganges with the river Humber near Marvell's hometown of Hull.

items.explanation: Günter Grass's novel The Tin Drum (Die Blechtrommel, 1959) famously opens with the narrator Oskar Matzerath writing his memoirs from his barred bed inside a mental hospital ('Granted: I am an inmate of a mental hospital...').

items.title: Mock #17 · Q70

items.explanation: In Robert Browning's dramatic monologue 'Andrea del Sarto' (1855), the 'Faultless Painter' wistfully acknowledges that although his technical draftsmanship exceeds Raphael's, Raphael possesses the burning 'soul' and visionary passion that Andrea lacks.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q72
items.stem: Who among the following were associated with Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood ?
options: Elizabeth Barrett Browning and Leigh Hunt
Dante Gabriel Rossetti and John Everett Millais
John Everett Millais and Elizabeth Barrett Browning
Dante Gabriel Rossetti and Leigh Hunt
items.explanation: Dante Gabriel Rossetti, John Everett Millais, and William Holman Hunt were the three principal founders of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood (PRB) established in London in 1848 to champion luminous realism, sincere expression, and detailed observation of nature.

items.explanation: The chronological sequence in which these critical theories emerged is: Psychoanalysis (late 1890s/1900 with Freud, B), New Criticism (1930s–1940s, E), Structuralism (1950s–1960s, A), Orientalism (1978 with Edward Said, D), and Ecocriticism (1990s, C), giving B, E, A, D, C.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q74
items.stem: Which Bible is the earliest English version printed with verse divisions ?
items.explanation: The Geneva Bible (1560), produced by English Protestant exiles in Geneva during the reign of Mary I, was the first complete English Bible to divide chapters into numbered verses and to be printed in Roman type.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q75
items.stem:
Which two of the following poems can be categorized as poems belonging to the neo-classical period of English literature.

(b) "The Vanity of Human Wishes"
(c) "Cato"
(d) "Lamia"
Choose the correct option:
items.explanation: Samuel Johnson's Juvenalian verse satire 'The Vanity of Human Wishes' (b, 1749) and Joseph Addison's verse tragedy Cato (c, 1713) belong to the eighteenth-century neoclassical period, whereas Keats's 'Lamia' (1820) is Romantic and Browning's The Ring and the Book (1868–69) is Victorian.

poems is a dramatic monologue ?
options: The Charge of the Light Brigade
items.explanation: Alfred, Lord Tennyson's 'Tithonus' (drafted in 1833, published in 1860) is a classical dramatic monologue in blank verse spoken by the Trojan prince Tithonus, who laments being granted immortal life without eternal youth by the dawn goddess Aurora.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q77

B. "Anaclisis" | II. Sigmund Freud
C. "Fetishism" | III. Alfred Binet

items.explanation: 'Habitus' is a sociological concept developed by Pierre Bourdieu (A-I), 'Anaclisis' (attachment of sexual drives to self-preservative instincts) was formulated by Sigmund Freud (B-II), psychological 'Fetishism' was coined by Alfred Binet in 1887 (C-III), and 'Hyperreality' was explored by Umberto Eco in Travels in Hyperreality (D-IV).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q78
items.stem: Who coined the term ”Phallogocentric”?
items.explanation: Jacques Derrida coined the portmanteau "phallogocentrism" by merging phallocentrism and logocentrism to deconstruct Western metaphysics for reinforcing male privilege alongside the illusion of unmediated speech.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The logical sequence for writing a research paper begins with Finding a Topic (B), followed by Gathering Data (A), Organizing Ideas and Setting Goals (D), Finding and Reading the Best Sources (C), and finally Writing the Paper (E), corresponding to Option 4: (B), (A), (D), (C), (E).

items.title: Mock #17 · Q80

Yeats's poems by publication year is: "Adam's Curse" (In the Seven Woods, 1903), "The Wild Swans at Coole" (1917), "The Second Coming" (1920/1921), "Among School Children" (The Tower, 1928), and his final poetic testament "Under Ben Bulben" (1938/1939). This sequence is A -> D -> C -> B -> E.

items.title: Mock #17 · Q91
items.stem:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:

What can be the use of a poetry that has no true subject except the poet's own selfhood? The traditional use of poetry in the Western world has been
instruction through delight, where teaching has meant the common truths or common deceptions of societal tradition, and where esthetic pleasure has
meant a fulfillment of expectations founded upon past joys of the same design.
But an individual psyche has its own accidents, which it needs to call truths, and its own necessity for self-recognition, which requires the pleasures of
originality, even if those pleasures depend upon a kind of lying against time, and against the achievements of the past. The use of such poetry demands to
be seen in a deidealized way, if it is to be seen more truly.
                                                                 - Harold Bloom, "The Use of Poetry"

options: The poet himself may be the subject
Poetry can have no true subject
Man may be the true subject of poetry
There can be no use of poetry
items.explanation: In 'The Use of Poetry' (from Figures of Capable Imagination, 1976), Harold Bloom observes that post-Enlightenment and Romantic lyric poetry takes the poet's own selfhood and individual psyche as its true subject.

Read the following poem and answer the questions that follow:

No worst, there is none.
No worst, there is none. Pitched past pitch of grief,
More pangs will, schooled at forepangs, wilder wring.
Comforter, where, where is your comforting?
Mary, mother of us, where is your relief?
My cries heave, herds-long; huddle in a main, a chief
Woe, world-sorrow; on an aage-old anvil wince and sing-
Then lull, then leave off. Fury had shrieked 'No lingering!
Let me be fell: force I must be brief."'
O the mind, mind has mountains; cliffs of fall
Frightful, sheer, no-man-fathomed. Hold them cheap
May who ne'er hung there. Nor does long our small
Durance deal with that steep or deep. Here! creep,
Wretch, under a comfort serves in a whirlwind: all
Life death does end and each day dies with sleep.
                                                                        - Gerard Manley Hopkins

Which of the following best describes the meaning of the title of the poem, 'No worst, there is none.'?
options: It is not worst because there is nothing
It is very bad as no one is there
No it is worst as nothing is there
Nothing can be so much bad as this
items.explanation: In Gerard Manley Hopkins's 'terrible sonnet' 'No worst, there is none' (composed 1885), the opening phrase expresses extreme spiritual anguish in which no suffering seems worse, yet even deeper pangs continually follow.

Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow:
'Justice' was done, and the President of the Immortals , in Aeschylean phrase, had ended his
sport with Tess. And the D'Urberville knights and dames slept on in their tombs unknowing.
The two speechless gazers bent themselves down to the earth, as if in prayer, and remained
thus a long time, absolutely motionless; the flag continued to wave silently. As soon as they
had enough strength they arose, joined hands again, and went on.
                                                                                                --Thomas Hardy, Tess of the D'Urbervilles
How did the 'sport with Tess' end?
items.explanation: At the close of Thomas Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles (1891), the raising of the black flag over Wintoncester prison signifies that Tess has been executed by hanging for killing Alec d'Urberville.

Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow:

The solemn temples, the great globe itself,
Yea, all which it inherit, shall dissolve
And, like this insubstantial pageant faded,
Leave not a rack behind. We are such stuff
As dreams are made on, and our little life
Is rounded with a sleep.
                                                                 --  Shakespeare, The Tempest
'[T]his insubstantial pageant' refers to:
items.explanation: In Act 4, Scene 1 of Shakespeare's The Tempest, Prospero's phrase 'this insubstantial pageant' refers immediately to the illusory betrothal masque performed by Ariel and his fellow spirits, which vanishes into thin air.
